verifier_note: Checked all 7 recipes by reading the docs.rs source mirror at pinned versions from the local cargo registry (midly-0.5.3, musicxml-1.1.2, quick-xml-0.42.0, roxmltree-0.21.1, abc-parser-0.4.0), cross-checked against oracle-jam/Cargo.toml (the actual wiring checks[] compile against), plus two compile_oracle.py counter-examples. All 14 cited source claims held up individually. Three recipes needed correction: recipe 3's engine_note wrongly treats 'Err-as-fatal' as equivalent to enabling midly's strict feature (Malformed is never raised without it); recipe 4 falsely calls quick-xml 0.42 'a no_std pull parser' (no such feature exists in its Cargo.toml or source); recipe 7's engine_note prescribes arithmetic on abc-parser's Length type that does not compile (no Mul impl, private field — confirmed E0369 and E0616 by counter-example). Systemic weakness: oracle-jam/Cargo.toml pins midly alone to match its recipe's recommended feature set (default-features=false, alloc); musicxml/quick-xml/roxmltree/abc-parser are all built with plain defaults, so any recipe recommending a non-default configuration for those four crates (recipe 4's musicxml default-features=false) can never be exercised end-to-end by this lane's own compile oracle -- only the crate's default happy path is ever mechanically checked, and that is exactly where the false and uncompilable claims clustered.

verdicts.verify_note: midly-0.5.3 Cargo.toml: default=[alloc,std,parallel]; parallel needs rayon. lib.rs: Smf unavailable w/o alloc. oracle-jam pins midly exactly as recipe recommends (default-features=false, features=[alloc]).

sources.note: 'Smf... unavailable without the alloc feature' -- exact match.

verdicts.verify_note: primitive.rs: Format{SingleTrack=0,Parallel=1,Sequential=2}, Timing{Metrical(u15),Timecode(Fps,u8)}; smf.rs Header{format,timing}. Hand-traced check bytes: header timing=0x0060 gives Metrical(96), matching stdout.
error.rs confirms Invalid/Malformed split, Malformed only emitted under strict. engine_note wrongly treats 'Err-as-fatal' as a substitute for strict -- without it, Malformed never raises Err at all.

corrections.claim: engine_note equates 'strict' with 'treating all Result::Err as fatal'; not equivalent. Without strict, ErrorKind::Malformed is never emitted (midly silently drops bad tracks/events per lib.rs), so Err-as-fatal alone only catches Invalid, missing what strict guards against.

sources.note: Invalid=fatal, Malformed=non-fatal unless strict -- exact match.
'plows through non-standard files... strict feature makes it reject' -- exact match.

verdicts.verify_note: musicxml lib.rs confirms no_std path + read_score_data_partwise (ungated). But 'what' falsely calls quick-xml 0.42 no_std (no such feature exists); oracle-jam pins musicxml w/ default std-on features, not default-features=false.

corrections.claim: 'what' calls quick-xml 0.42 'a no_std pull parser' -- false: its Cargo.toml has no std/no_std/alloc feature (default=[]); lib.rs unconditionally does 'use std::borrow::Cow'. Also the check links musicxml with default (std-on) features, not the recipe's own recommended default-features=false.
